chapter: Return to New Orleans and Preservation Hall
title: Return to New Orleans, Jaffe takes over Preservation Hall, Kid Thomas band
summary: He returned in 1948, then went back to Chicago; talks of the Hall's ownership, concert tours and joining the Kid Thomas band.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Then you came back to New Orleans and you stayed there.

Yeah, and then I, the second while I had, we would be together, then we'd separate, and we'd come back together, and I just, I came out to visit, and my people had bought a place on Corneyes Street, and I came, when I went back, the Dland later died, so I stayed about a week more at the Bell Range, her funeral and everything, and I came back in 48, all the way up until 65, and I went to take Mike's place after Chad Limited. I stayed there three years. And things was awful around, Chicago music, man.
How was it down here when you came back in?
Well things were problems with Preservation Hall, old mufflers, old mufflers, a lot of guys down here. I don't know, I'll say 60, me. Some people say 62. Well the Jaffees took over in 62.
Yeah, well that's when he took it over.
They had Bernstein, and then they had another lady with him, and then another little fellow from California, a cripple, right?

And that's when Jaffees did him, was going up I think at Tulane University, because you see, we used to play for all of them way back there, Tulane University. And then they took it over, and it's been successful ever since. That's probably about like 62, like you said. Then they started having concerts, you see, the first one, Iowa, was in Japan, yeah, in 19... No, I went somewhere because I was with George Lou's band, yeah. We played some old Cincinnati, and then St. Paul, the Twin Cities, and a couple other places, some places in Virginia, you see. So, after George's band, George died, and the band held for a little while, and then went down with... Then they took over the band, you see. And they pushed him when Willie got in there, you see. And I got a record to me, but that was made in the Twin Cities. And I recorded with Punch Miller, and all of them. Punch Miller was pretty good. And so, then they put me in with the... The Kid Thomas band, because they had a concert tour, and Charlie's wife was a piano, but their wife was sick, and he decided that... Bless the world, because I couldn't make it. So they put me in the band, and I didn't know I was going to stay in the band. When I came, we'd come back off the concert tour. I found, they'd say, come in tonight, you know, come in tonight. Next week, come in tonight, same night, so I'd stay here.
